paragraphs: The V250/V250d has been part of the V-Class range since the W447 generation launched in 2014, and the model received a major refresh alongside the Vito for 2025. Earlier W447 models use the OM651 - a 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel shared across a wide range of Mercedes vehicles of that era. From the 2025 refresh, the V250/V250d switched to the OM654 - a newer 2.0-litre diesel that's a different unit entirely, not an evolution of the OM651. Knowing which one your van has matters, because the components and the known wear patterns differ between them - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every V250 V250D on the road.

cards.body: A 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to the V250/V250d from the W447 launch in 2014 through to the 2025 refresh. Known for injector seal leaks and timing chain wear - see the callout above. We replace timing chain components, injector seals, EGR, and gaskets as standard on every OM651 rebuild.

The current 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel, fitted from the 2025 refresh onward. A genuinely different design from the OM651 - no specific known issues independently confirmed for this application at this stage, though we service it to the same rigorous standard as our other V-Class rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the V250/V250d spans two distinct engines across the W447 generation, fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming an OM651 part will work on an OM654 van - risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic V-Class quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
